title: Strict lifting of a reduced map into an acyclic complex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $K$ a bounded-above complex of projective $R$-modules, and $A$ any $R$-complex. Let $C$ be an acyclic $R/I$-complex and $e:(R/I)\otimes_R A\cong C$ an isomorphism of complexes. Every map $\iota:(R/I)\otimes_R K\to C$ has a strict lift $f:K\to A$ satisfying $((R/I)\otimes_R f)\circ e=\iota$, with composition in diagrammatic order. No acyclicity or boundedness of $A$ is required.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 0BCA, dotted-arrow paragraph, using the null-homotopy into the acyclic cone

proof.text: The reduced K is bounded above because extension of scalars preserves zero objects. Its terms are projective by the extension/restriction adjunction, whose right adjoint preserves epimorphisms. Therefore reduced K is K-projective and the map to acyclic C has a homotopy H to zero.

The adjunction unit from an R-module to its restricted reduction is surjective: TensorProduct.mk_surjective applies since the quotient ring map is surjective. For each component of H composed with e inverse, use the adjunction and projectivity of the K term to factor it through this unit. Adjunction naturality shows that the resulting component reduces, followed by e, to H.

Take Homotopy.nullHomotopicMap of this lifted family. Compatibility with additive functors and postcomposition identifies its reduction followed by e with nullHomotopicMap H.hom. The defining homotopy equation gives precisely the supplied map.
